Perfume rating 4.34 out of 5 with 2,830 votes

Nio by Xerjoff is a Woody Spicy fragrance for men. Nio was launched in 2009. Top notes are Bergamot, Green Notes and Neroli; middle notes are Cardamom, Pink Pepper, Jasmine and Nutmeg; base notes are Vetyver, Virginia Cedar, Guaiac Wood, Amber and Patchouli.

Nio perfume from the Shooting Stars Collection is a refreshing stroll through the southern Italian countryside. Rich and tasty Calabria bergamot and neroli are mixed with mysterious spicy notes of cardamom, nutmeg and pink pepper. This unique combination is blended with a dry woody base of cedar and Guaiac wood, Haiti vetiver, amber and Indian patchouli to create a timeless blend of romantic memories. Nio is a lasting example of elegance and style.

> It is available as 50 and 100 ml EDP.

This fragrance immediately takes me to a wooden dock on a quiet lake. The afternoon sun filters through the trees, warming the planks beneath me, while a cool breeze carries the scent of water as it dries from my skin. Fish dart through the vegetation nearby, completing the scene.

I absolutely love this one.

StarA2 09/03/25 17:02

When I consider the Nio fragrance from Xerjoff, I feel a mix of admiration and deep reflection. The scent takes me on a refreshing summer journey, as if I’m strolling through the southern Italian countryside, where Calabrian bergamot and neroli blend with gentle breezes carrying pure green notes. I enjoy its citrusy opening, which merges with mysterious spicy touches of cardamom, nutmeg, and pink pepper, before settling into a warm woody base of cedar, Haitian vetiver, amber, and patchouli, creating unforgettable romantic scent memories. I consider it a classic fragrance ideal for neroli lovers, and while using it, I appreciate its clear sillage and strong longevity, lasting around seven hours. However, deep down, I find its scent lacks the uniqueness I crave, resembling other market fragrances, which leads me to question whether its high price is justified, especially since I’ve discovered similar designer alternatives at a much lower cost. Still, I rate it personally 7/10 as one of the most balanced and beautiful summer scents, but my experience with it led me to buy it only once, without repurchasing, perhaps because I’m seeking something more distinctive within the Xerjoff range.

I love this summer stunner.

The fresh greenness that this gives off for hours is so real, mature and different. The sharp bergamot mixed with neroli hits me so well, words can not give it justice. I would simply say imagine walking through a row of lemon trees with the winding whipping the greenness of the citrus trees around you. As it dries down, that sharp green citrus blends with a nice Vetiver making for a great trio of notes.

For a fresh greenness citrus fragrance, the longevity is above average. 6/7 hours on skin…longer on clothes. Projection is moderate from the get go…but it pushes that way for a few hours before working its way back.

This is not your typical commercial fresh summer fragrance. I can see how some people could dislike the sharpness and green nature of this fragrance. I would highly recommend getting a sample of this before going in on a bottle.

gradylives 09/02/24 16:48

This is probably the most visually evocative frag in my collection.

Picture walking up to a nice orange grove, with the fruit just about ripe, and ready to pick.
There's a lot of fresh grass and leaves around you, and it's around 11am or so.
You sit down for a few minutes to eat an orange and enjoy your surroundings.

Now put all of that in a bottle, and you have the opening of Nio.

It really does smell like a day in an orange grove in the opening, and if that opening could stay around longer, I'd definitely keep a bottle of this in my collection, and I'd consider this a classic.

As it is, tho, it's eventually turns more green...evoking spring grass and leaves on the breeze.
You go from sitting in an orange grove, to sitting on a hillside under a tree about 30 minutes to an hour in.
It's still very pleasant, and enjoyable, but for me, the shift from such an amazing photorealistic citrus is a little disappointing.
I'd imagine citrus notes are tough to keep in the air for extended periods of time, so I understand the change, but still...
Eventually it dries down to a very nice, smooth, woody scent.
It's a great spring/summer scent BUT I probably won't buy a second bottle.
The opening is absolutely amazing, and frankly, really damn cool (I got no idea how to get SUCH a realistic smell in a bottle), but the rest of the experience cant live up to it, IMO.
I'd recommend getting your nose on it, if you can. Maybe the experience will be different for you, and the opening is a thing of beauty

Citrusy, green, spicy, fresh, woody, and slightly soapy. This is a fan favorite for a good reasons. It's hard to go wrong with this combo.

I wouldn't say it'll necessarily impress anyone, like some more mysterious and deeper Xerjoff fragrances does. But you'll definitely smell clean and fresh with a bit of a kick. The spice really do hit nicely and takes it from "hot weather only" to a spring, summer, and autumn fragrance. Projects fine, doesn't get too clawing, but has a presence. This is all ocations worthy. Dressed up or casual. I'd go as far as to say it's a wedding scent, if you're trying to not take the spotlight from the couple getting married. It does have class. But not in an uptight way. Easy to wear, all day, or even for a warm summer night.

If you like XJ 1861 Renaissance, but would like less citrus dominance and no mint, this might be your jam right here. I personally prefer Renaissance, but would not regret a full bottle of Nio either.

Personal score: 8.5/10. A solid Xerjoff for most ocations.
I'd call it blind buy safe if you like the notes.

Update (7/13/2024): Re-review after using up my sample on a hot day. I've changed my rating to OK. Nio is too green for me and not enough citrus. I won't be getting a full bottle.

This is my second fresh/summer Xerjoff I've tested. The first was Fiero which was an easy 5 star thumbs up. Nio is a bit more complicated. First the definite positive - this is a very long lasting (longer than Fiero) summer freshie. For me, sillage was moderate for a few hours but even down to a skin scent there was a definite scent bubble around me. I got a good 12+ hours out of it. At the end, it was still a noticeable and moderate skin scent.

Now the complicated part - the opening. For me, this is more of a green/fresh fragrance than citrus/fresh. The opening green is quite strong and after a few minutes I definitely got a laundry detergent vibe. That didn't last long (maybe 10 minutes). In the air (to myself and others) it comes across as a fresh, green scent. Getting up close to my skin, there's a definite pickled scent. It immediately reminded me of the pickled sport peppers used in Chicago style hot dogs. The pickled scent gradually diminished and by the hour mark was completely gone. What remained was a great woody/earthy scent with a subtle green accent.

My final rating is a like but I'm not ready to buy a FB yet due to the price and going with Fiero which I liked better. I strongly recommend to anyone wanting to try Nio that you plan to apply it 1 hour before going out/meeting with others. Once it's settled, it's really nice but that first hour can be challenging.

TBonetheFella 05/12/24 15:20

An early morning brunch picnic with friends in a park on a bright and sunny summers day. The smell of the fresh dew on the grass, leaves, wildflowers and various greens mixes with the citrus sparkling water you all drink. Good times and laughs are had as you all discuss the plans for later in the night. Life is good.

Bright, juicy, realistic, and sparkling bergamot, clean neroli, and green, stemmy dew smack you across the face as soon as you spray this. Green. Clean. Fresh. Uplifting. As it dries it gains a wonderful cedar, guaiac, and vetiver woody backbone as cardamom, nutmeg, and pepper deepen the freshness with some spice beyond just a squeeze of citrus and a splash of green.

This is one of those fragrances that I wish I could just smell the opening over and over again. It's so bright, clean, realistic and refreshing that it always brings a smile to my face. That being said, the realistic bergamot and green combo could come off too sharp for those not expecting it when smelling it up close, but this SINGS in the heat. Overpriced for what it is, but what it does: it does really really well. Super versatile, can wear this casual or formal, but pushes better off me in outdoor situations than indoor situations.

Long lasting performance for a freshie with respectably powerful projection under heat. Don't expect this to push without heat.

8.8/10 (can see this going higher this summer)

Song vibe - Blue Skies by Moxie


Side note: The only reason people think this smells like Artisan Pure by JV is because it's primarily a bitter citrus mixed with a predominant green note. AP doesn't have that clean white neroli, nor vetiver which are both super prominent in here.

Have you ever read a press release from, say, Dolce & Gabanna, heralding the Mediterranean inspiration of a new fragrance? It’s probably described as a robust citrus garden you’ll be happy to smell like and include too much hyperbole. Xerjoff’s Nio, however, is a fragrance that truly delivers on that type of hype. Bergamot and Neroli are the two key halves of Nio and they combine to create a tart and floral sensation that is oh so serene.

I get the occasional spicy element within Nio, but really, the fragrance stays pretty linear. Sure, other elements emerge as the scent dries down. Jasmine begins to compliment the neroli and Nio takes on a more white floral character with green herbal undertones that may leave you feeling freshly pollinated. Yet it still remains close to the opening and wears like a fantastic vacation. As I’ve come to expect from Xerjoff, performance is equally fantastic.

Wearing Nio is like spending the day in the most tranquil place imaginable. Given the amount of uncertainly in the world at any time, that’s a sensation to really be thankful for and I offer Nio my tasteful applause.

JusttheFactsMan 12/11/23 06:42

#480 in my "Tour de Fragrance"

After trying out nearly 500 fragrances I find myself wanting to smell something that I don't find myself saying "I've been here before." If you check out the "reminds me of" you'll see there is no consensus on what Xerjoff Nio smells like. The reason there's no agreement is that this fragrance doesn't smell just like anything. One sniff you think you think it's something powdery like Dior Homme Intense. Another sniff and you think it's something woody and spicy like Cool Water, Aspen, or even GIT. But it doesn't really remind you of any of those.

The notes in this scent are all common enough to dozens of masculine fragrances (and this is an unmistakably masculine scent), but emphasizing the pink pepper, as they do here, is not something you often smell. Maison Margiela's "Replica By the Fireplace" and "Jazz Club" also hit the pepper note hard, but its concealed by more prominent notes like cashmere and vanilla. I now realize that what I find unique and attractive in those Fragrances is exactly how hard they're hitting the pink pepper. I really like that peppery edge and Nio's got it!

Nio is fine for carpool, elevator, office, formal or casual wear. Very versatile and good for any season except the bitterest cold of Winter. But the primary reason I'm going to shell out the money for a full bottle of this is that I know this is not something everyone will have smelled on a dozen men before me. It comes off clean, vibrant, crisp like a lightly starched dress shirt you just picked up at the laundry. But it's attractively uncommon. And chances are if you're wearing this as your go-to scent, it's a fragrance they will associate with you and you alone, when every barista, Best Buy sales associate, and guy from the mailroom is wearing Sauvage.

Cullin 02/23/23 08:02

Gosh I love this juice as a citrus lover. This is one of the most realistic, natural smelling citrus fragrance I have ever smelled along with AC's Orange Sanguine. Bergamot dominant, with lots of neroli and greenness. The spices blend really well with the bergamot/neroli greenness combo, but I don't think this is a spicy fragrance at all. It's all about the bergamot, neroli and the greenness to the end. Vibrant and sharp. Summer/Spring superstar. Casual but could also be worn during weddings/summer time dates etc. Packacing is top tier as a Xerjoff product. This fragrance makes me want to hop in my Mercedes Benz W126 during a summer vacation, drive to the beach, and just relax.

However this fragrance has pretty moderate performance considering it is a parfum concenctration (31% oils). It only lasts about 5-7 hours on my skin. Projects really well for the first hour and half (3-5 feet), then gets a bit closer to the skin (1-3 feet). At 3-4 hour mark it still projects a little, but then it pretty much turns into a skin scent, and stays a a skin scent for two or three more hours or so. I wish it lasted like solid 7-9 hours on my skin but it sadly won't. Some people have better performance, and they get over 8 hours with it. My bottle is 2 years, and two months old. If you could find this on a sale for like 150-170 bucks then I think it will be worth it (if you love citrus, neroli, greenness type of thing).

Summary; I love this fragrance, and the mood boost I get from smelling this. The moderate longevity/projection for a parfum concentration fragrance is still a bit annoying thing about this. Also the price tag could be quite lower considering the performance.

Scent: 10/10
Longevity: 6.5/10 5-7 hours
Projection/Sillage: 7/10 (great projection for the first 1.5-3 hours)
Price: 3/10 (Retail price is too high considering the longevity/performance, but totally worth it if you can find it on a sale)
Uniqueness: 9/10
Personal liking: 9/10

Edit after few months and uses; I find it more spicy now in the background, giving this some night time aspect, meaning that this could be used during evening/night time on warmer weather. Also the projection is better than I thought. Performance is pretty good for a citrus freshie. Absolutely fantastic fragrance.

Pro_96 12/30/22 05:08

Generally, packaging doesn’t matter all that much when it comes to fragrances, but I feel like Xerjoff’s packaging deserves a praise or two. In my opinion, they have the best packaging & presentation of any brand. Extremely premium, worth retaining & they give a piece of a meteorite with some of the fragrances in their ‘Shooting Stars’ line, which is quite fantastic.

Anyone who knows Xerjoff would be aware of Nio, as it is one of the fragrances that made Xerjoff popular. Launched back in 2009, many have described this perfume as a masterpiece, and I can see why. Nio is a citrus heavy fragrance which would shine on a hot day, under the sun and is ideal for summer. The quality and blend of the ingredients used in Nio are excellent. There’s nothing synthetic about it. The opening is dominated by bergamot and Neroli, which are extremely photorealistic. Once it dries down, it transforms into a green, woody scent and the Jasmine and vetiver come out, and if one likes green fragrances, this would be something they love. This smells/feels like sitting under a lemon tree under the sun. In the air, this just smells beautiful.

If Green Irish Tweed is a walk by the Irish countryside, then Nio is a picnic beside a lemon orchard in the Italian countryside.

The projection is quite moderate with this one, but due to the nature of its smell, it can get way too much, too fast. The longevity on this one is about 5 - 5.5 hours, which isn’t excellent, considering the price of the fragrance. However, given the nature of citrus based fragrances, and natural ingredients, it is quite understandable. If I had to dock points for anything in this fragrance, it would be the longevity.

This is not a fragrance which one should blind buy, unless you know what it is you are looking for. This is not a scent that everyone will love. People who are used to designers and people who are looking for appreciation of others, should look elsewhere. If one does not have a mature nose or does not enjoy citrusy or green fragrance, this is not for them. This is a scent for those who love citrus based fragrances and are looking for the best citrus fragrances with the most natural, highest quality ingredients in it; and for people who want that, this is what you’re looking for. This is a perfume one wears for themselves, and it is ideal for special occasions. It can also be pulled off during the night, if it is warm enough. It is a treat for the senses.

I would give it a solid 9/10, as the projection is not the best in the world. However, it is the best citrus based fragrance I’ve smelled.

Chesco 01/13/22 11:52

Blind Buy Bottle

Same packaging, but this time it came with a small envelope within the coffret, and inside that was 2 meteorite rocks with a certificate from Siberia Russia that landed in 1947. :S

2 sprays, opening was a strong blast of lemon and some kind of grassy green note, first thing that came to mind was a uncommon cooking herb and Layton Exclusive.
After that it moves to a realistic citrus bergamot lime mixed with a laundry soap floral note, and altho this is a strong scent, it's added so delicately that the dna of this frag is elegant. You can definitely smell the neroli mixed with the laundry soap note. An image of clean sheets hits my brain when smelling this frag. This is a freshy, and elegantly done!
There are not a lot of notes in this frag, it's kept simple, with quality ingredients, clean, fresh, and refreshing - it's a very elegant beautiful dna.
The citrus acid from the bergamot is a main player here, as is a fizzy white musk, and it's blended beautifully, and less harsh than the one's you find in Creed Silver Mountain Water/Aventus.
There is just a sprinkle of a spicy pepper here, i can go along with the note pyramid and agree that it's a pink peppercorn but i can't be for sure unless i was in the lab making it to confirm.
Im not getting any cardamom.
But i am getting a hint of grassy-dryness, and im guessing that it's from the Vetiver.
The note of Jasmine comes into play but soooo lightly added, you can hardly tell apart from the Neroli floral.
There is also a slight hint of metallic in the bottom while sniffing, that hits the back of the nose.
Also, it has a slight kitchen cleaner vibe to it's scent to it due to a note of lemon, ruined by the cleaning industry.

I do have a very strong issue with this frag. If one was to love it, they would wear it all the time and because it's a freshy, people tend to use a couple extra sprays so it can project. Selling at only a 50ml bottle and at the insane price they are asking since the ingredients are so minimal and it's a freshie, i personally don't think this fragrance is worth it unless you're a hardcore frag head and/or collector. I paid after a nice discount $180 CND for this 50ml (so $360 for a normal sized 100ml bottle), for a freshy that's over-priced as well as the competition of freshies selling at such a economical value in it's scent genre.
If this was selling at $200 CND for a 100ml bottle id say that would be a much fairer price to the customer, then id strongly recommend this to everyone. Paying like $360 CND if this came in a 100ml normal sized bottle for a laundry detergent soap main note is wrong imo, and it actually makes me feel a lil upset inside when using any sprays of my 50ml bottle. If they are using a laundry soap to make this it shouldn't have such a huge pricetag that they are currently selling a small bottle at.

But, that being said, to date i have yet to smell any freshie of this one-up quality. And if you're really into freshies, i will also say that this is a must-have.
To date, this is the most beautiful freshie i've ever smelt. The price kills my heart... I kinda wish i didn't like it so i can resell the bottle to get my money back, but i think it's too beautiful to give away...
Wearing this daily is like you're either rich or a irresponsible person just burning through money.
100% this is going to be my wedding fragrance, it's absolutely perfect for a wedding day!!
And with that all said, this goes straight to the top of my opinion of the top 5 best fragrances i've smelt to date from the x10 blind-buy bottles within the Xerjoff line.
If this came in a 100ml size and was selling for around the $200 price tag, id buy it and wear it often.
I've decided to sell my bottle, because i disagree with the pricing of it's offering. It really is made with refined/distilled laundry detergent with a lemon note added, and i can't live with myself paying it's price for only 50ml.

4/5 Woofs!

Asking for opinions from people with no fragrance experience, everyone thought the very opening reminded them of toilet cleaner. It's such an intense blast of bergamot. After it calms down a bit, everyone started liking it more and thought it reminded them of a really expensive Nordic hotel. Or a pine forest in the summer. Generally everyone said it was unique and high-class. Quite serious and somewhat mature.

Despite not liking this personally, I have to give credit for the performance, quality and concentration! This is by far the longest-lasting citrus fragrance I've ever tried. FMilan 08/15/21 18:15

I had nothing to do today and I went on a brief search to try and find out the lemon used as reference on Nio.

To me, it seems to be one of the variations of citrus aurantifolia - and it's not the regular key lime most people know - but one closely related to it: we called it here in Brasil "limão galego" (galician lemon, in a literal translation) - it's smaller, with a thin and yellow-ish peel and not as acid as (sicilian) lemon or the regular lime (that we know here as "limão tahiti").

I thought, at first, that it was "limão cravo" (citrus limonia), aka "rangpur", that is also small, sweeter and has an orange and kinda rugged peel when ripe.

It's a citrus fragrance, fair and square, with a leafy (lemon leaf) and slightly peppery background, that gives it the extra sour flavour. It dries down woody, but always green and citric.

I would not call it the best, but surely one the most realistic citrus fragrances out there. Bergamote 22 is as realistic (having bergamot as reference) but not as good as Nio. Acqua di Parma Essenza has the most realistic neroli, but it's a little "buried" in the blend.

Even if I don't love it, I can't say it's not a 10/10. It is.

JusttheFactsMan 12/11/23 06:42

#480 in my "Tour de Fragrance"

After trying out nearly 500 fragrances I find myself wanting to smell something that I don't find myself saying "I've been here before." If you check out the "reminds me of" you'll see there is no consensus on what Xerjoff Nio smells like. The reason there's no agreement is that this fragrance doesn't smell just like anything. One sniff you think you think it's something powdery like Dior Homme Intense. Another sniff and you think it's something woody and spicy like Cool Water, Aspen, or even GIT. But it doesn't really remind you of any of those.

The notes in this scent are all common enough to dozens of masculine fragrances (and this is an unmistakably masculine scent), but emphasizing the pink pepper, as they do here, is not something you often smell. Maison Margiela's "Replica By the Fireplace" and "Jazz Club" also hit the pepper note hard, but its concealed by more prominent notes like cashmere and vanilla. I now realize that what I find unique and attractive in those Fragrances is exactly how hard they're hitting the pink pepper. I really like that peppery edge and Nio's got it!

Nio is fine for carpool, elevator, office, formal or casual wear. Very versatile and good for any season except the bitterest cold of Winter. But the primary reason I'm going to shell out the money for a full bottle of this is that I know this is not something everyone will have smelled on a dozen men before me. It comes off clean, vibrant, crisp like a lightly starched dress shirt you just picked up at the laundry. But it's attractively uncommon. And chances are if you're wearing this as your go-to scent, it's a fragrance they will associate with you and you alone, when every barista, Best Buy sales associate, and guy from the mailroom is wearing Sauvage.
